# Addressing scenario cards
S1:192.168.50.70/27 and192.168.50.100/27 share three octets. Explain why this does not make them local to each other.
S2: six endpoints are given /29 and gateway first host. Explain the capacity fault.
S3: Staff is assigned192.168.50.32/27 while Media uses192.168.50.0/26. Identify overlap and repair the allocation.
S4: a gateway is listed as 192.168.50.95 for a.70/27 host. Explain why it is unsuitable in this ordinary LAN plan.
S5:10.1.18.200/20 is wrongly described as network 10.1.18.0. Show the relevant mask octet and correct range .
S6: a documentation address is called public because it is not RFC 1918. Correct the scope reasoning.
S7: an IPv6 address contains two :: compressions. Explain ambiguity and how to write an unambiguous address.
S8: a /64 IPv6 subnet is assigned usable count2^64−2. Explain why that copies an IPv4 convention incorrectly.
Use original hypothetical diagrams/data; no school network access or configuration is required.
